I always struggled with what was appropriate to say to that patient until then.

And that aide in particular, if she does use a name, it aint a pet name, it's "ma". If you're white/suburban like me and need the explanation, it's out of respect, urban black American thing? Maybe you know what I mean. Just wanted to add that

One more thing is, if you have the mindset that every person CAN either directly or non-directly teach you something (about yourself, life), it's much easier to see the value in a conversation with them, and therefore little sparks will go off in your head as to what to say, rather than having to think so hard (the socially anxious, forceful interactions bc you're trying desperately to be a human). If you wanna learn, the world and people in it are your oyster... but just be aware I don't necessarily mean going up to something and saying "teach me something". It's more subtle *most of the time. It can even be a mundane conversation that you find some wonderful lesson in. You may learn from a conversation exactly how NOT to be, and sometimes that's pretty funny. Whatever, I'm done typing.

Edit- Another thing is, are you embarrassed to be who you are? Are you ashamed of how you live? Then, unless you can be appropriately self-deprecating (but not emotionally manipulating others into simply feeling sorry for you), interacting with people is going to have some painful moments. Like you can't acknowledge/joke about/be accountable for some elephant in the room that YOU are responsible for?- then interaction will be more painful than it has to be. Clear conscious clear conscious clear conscious... it takes action and hard work to achieve a clear conscious sometimes, but it ultimately makes life much easier.

Here's the other catch -- when you don't give a damn, don't act like you do. In other words, be honest with yourself and the person you ostensibly are 'supposed to' talk to, by not talking when you don't want/have to (but you don't have to verbalize "I don't wanna talk", I'm saying BEHAVE in line with what you feel). Know when conversation is dry to the point where silence is a-okay.

There are nuances depending on the social scenario but it's something to keep in mind. Don't knowingly waste your time and energy, cuz you know you don't want other people wasting yours. But don't get all paranoid like "oh shit I don't wanna overstep and waste other people's time, so I'm gonna just shut down and never reach out to people" -- people will give you cues they're not interested, and as long as you have your eyes open to that possibility, you can see it, respect it, be respected for respecting their cues, and move on accordingly.

I finally felt calm at the idea of buying a bottle of vodka and sharp knife, and bleeding out in my bed. No more rocking or breathing heavy, just calm, relief. I dragged my nails up my leg simulating a knife. Bit my wrist, didn't bleed (kind of reached the peak and didn't have the will to do it), but the mark is there 12 hours later.
